description: How good it is to be near God. That is not a quiet observation. That is a burst of joy from someone who has actually experienced His presence.
excerpt: Being close to God and being covered by God changes what comes out of our mouths. If we are truly close to Him, and truly sheltered by Him, we cannot help but talk about Him. It leaks out.
verse: "But as for me, how good it is to be near God! I have made the Sovereign Lord my shelter, and I will tell everyone about the wonderful things you do."
body_html:
I love the exclamation point in this verse.

How good it is to be near God!

That is not a quiet observation. That is not a polite little statement. That is a burst of joy. You can almost hear the writer saying it out loud. Like he cannot contain how good it feels to be close to Him.

When was the last time we talked about being near God like that?

We say a lot of things about God. He is faithful. He is loving. He is powerful. All true. But there is something different about saying how good it is to be near Him. That is personal. That is intimate. That is the language of someone who has actually experienced His presence and cannot get over it.

David does not just say he is near God. He says he has made the Sovereign Lord his shelter. That takes it a step further. Being near is one thing. Being under is another.

Shelter is where you go when you need protection. When the storm rolls in. When you are exhausted. When you are exposed. When you have nowhere else safe to land. Shelter is a covering.

And David chose God as his.

He didn't choose his career. Or his wealth. Or his family. Not his own strength. God was his shelter. The one he ran to. The one he lived under. The one who covered him when everything else could not.

Then the verse ends with an action.

I will tell everyone about the wonderful things you do.

Being close to God and being covered by God changes what comes out of our mouths.

We can talk about what we love. If we are truly close to God, and truly sheltered by Him, we cannot help but talk about Him. It leaks out. It shows up in our conversations. It comes up when someone asks about our week. It bubbles into our stories.

Which begs the question.

When is the last time you told anyone a wonderful thing God has done?

Not in church. Not in a prayer request group. Not to another Christian who was expecting to hear something spiritual.

Actually anyone. A neighbor. A coworker. The person next to you at the coffee shop. Your kids in the car. A friend who is not walking with God. Someone who did not think they were going to hear the name of Jesus that day.

Because if we are close to Him, and if He is our shelter, and if He is doing wonderful things, then not telling anyone is a little strange when you think about it.

Something worth wondering about.
question: If you had to name the last wonderful thing God did in your life, could you? And who could you tell about it today?
